faq.a: Atef is associated with the Arabic form عَاطِف, whose core sense is atef; affectionate, sympathetic.

faq.q: What is the origin of Atef?
faq.a: Atef is associated with Arabic. Atef is Arabic عَاطِف (ʿĀṭif), the active participle of عَطَفَ, meaning 'affectionate, sympathetic'.
Yes — the underlying form عَاطِف is Arabic.
Atef can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Atef should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. ʿĀṭif is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Atef mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Atef is rendered عاطف and carries the sense عاطف، مہربان.

faq.q: What does Atef mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Atef is rendered عاطف and carries the sense عاطف، مهربان.
A romanized syllable approximation is a-tef. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Atef?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Atef, atef. Script forms are عاطف, عَاطِف, आतिफ़.

faq.q: Is Atef a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
